sourceBackedScope.text: The examples support a broad parent with distinct branches for effective actions, flux-vacuum existence, de Sitter instability, geometric gauge realization and infinite-distance behavior. Add the N=2 rigid-limit candidate under a separate gauge–gravity-scale question. Route plateau inflation to cosmology and leave spacetime topology change outside. These are candidate navigation choices across related questions, not evidence for a common physical mechanism.

scopeLimits.text: The effective-action studies distinguish warped type-II N=1 SU(3)×SU(3) backgrounds from Calabi–Yau N=2 reductions. In the latter, magnetic charges induce a massive two-form, and symplectic covariance requires transforming the flux vector. Quantized fluxes appear as continuous parameters only in the low-energy description.

The flux discussion mainly treats conventional IIA/M-theory without boundaries or O8-planes; its constraints need not assume supersymmetry. It states no precise no-go theorem for scale-separated AdS. The de Sitter search instead tests sufficient tachyon conditions in two- and four-field sectors, without establishing full stability or string control.

The 5d coupling argument uses the cubic prepotential without string/M-theory input; the GV comparison uses M-theory on Calabi–Yau threefolds. Their reported agreement supports the Emergent String Conjecture in the tested examples. The nilpotent/global-symmetry and tower-induced-distance interpretations remain motivations, not demonstrated general mechanisms.

The plateau model's supergravity-inspired label supplies no compactification construction here. cases.prompt: I want to understand how an inflationary model connects its potential and field trajectory to observables, reheating, and quantum-gravity consistency.
cases.reviewedTitle: Inflation and scalar dark-sector cosmology: observations and theoretical consistency

sourceBackedScope.text: The sampled core supports a parent with separate inflation, equality-era scalar-decay and quintessence branches. Within inflation, particle relic production, PBH formation, potential-flatness tuning and strong-coupling signatures answer distinct questions. This hierarchy supports comparisons of observational and theoretical constraints while preserving different mechanisms, epochs and evidential status.

scopeLimits.text: Viability remains relative to each paper's data and model. Inflaton-decay relic production carries stability, BBN and Lyman-α restrictions. Supergravity tuning concerns relative couplings that flatten the potential, distinct from its overall scale. Interrupted monodromy includes strong-coupling kinetic corrections; its chiral-wave signal additionally assumes an axion–dark-photon coupling.

Ultralight-scalar decay operates near matter–radiation equality with a potential quadratic near its minimum. The observational assessment uses an effective fluid approximation. Rapid transfer requires a large coupling; a concrete UV realization and an explanation of the transition's timing remain unresolved.

The quintessence gradient test is conjectural and concerns V > 0 and the physical scalar-field gradient. Its order-one coefficient conflicts with the fifth-force-limited slope in this example; the light/heavy-mass-ratio alternative is attributed to an unsupplied work. The separate stable-AdS premise lacks its precise domain, stability criteria and supersymmetry qualifications.

sampledDistinctions.text: Near-inflection potentials serve different dark-matter questions. Inflaton decay produces nonthermal fermions in one example; enhanced curvature fluctuations lead to radiation-era gravitational collapse into PBHs in the other. Shared potential shape supports comparison without identifying the production mechanisms.

Axion–gauge-field dynamics provides a useful bridge between inflationary chiral-wave production and equality-era dark radiation. The epochs, energy scales and target observables differ. The ultralight-scalar source explicitly invokes a preheating analogy, which does not make its Hubble-tension question an inflation question.

AdS denotes a bulk hosting a cosmological bubble, a stable vacuum excluded by an incompletely specified premise, or an asymptotic supersymmetric regime. These windows establish neither a contradiction among those uses nor a common consistency criterion. The bubble papers share a setting while asking different nucleation and perturbation questions.

cases.prompt: For several axions, how do I identify the physical light direction and decide whether integrating out the heavier fields is justified?
requiredDistinctions: canonical kinetic normalization versus unnormalized coordinate range
mass eigenvectors versus assumed light direction
cases.reviewedTitle: Axion kinetic normalization, masses and conditional light-field reduction

sourceBackedScope.text: The sources support a method core of kinetic normalization and mass/mixing analysis, with light-field reduction conditional on the model. The aligned-LVS outside candidate directly fits this core and clarifies why an illustrative reduced potential need not replace two-field cosmological dynamics. Thermal scalar averaging and infrared spinodal flattening perform different operations. Some descriptions include steps absent from their supplied anchors; supported membership does not certify those additional clauses.

scopeLimits.text: Normalization uses chosen or stabilized moduli. The heterotic parameter choices remain illustrative rather than derived for a specified compactification. The quintessence example fixes saxions and uses a mass hierarchy near a saddle; its effective theory requires weak coupling, large volume and moduli masses below string and Kaluza–Klein scales.

The universal-axion K⁻¹V calculation retains leading volume and small shift-breaking scalings around an LVS minimum, without exact coefficients. Its natural-inflation regime f>M_Pl entails g_s>1, outside the perturbative regime used to compute the theory. Suggested volume suppression does not establish control of all higher corrections.

The CP-based abundance estimate assumes an inflationary axion mass of order H and a small initial offset. The quoted abundance formula applies to the stated scenario without light moduli, with reheating well above QCD and an axion-plus-radiation postinflationary universe. The authors assign uncertainties of perhaps an order of magnitude.

sampledDistinctions.text: Kinetic scales, axion periods and alignment-enhanced effective decay constants are distinct. The FDM passage qualifies its kinetic decay-constant convention for massless axions. In aligned LVS, metric rotations also transform the charges, so canonical coordinates need not individually have periods 2πf_i.

The quintessence example removes a stable heavy direction near a saddle using its mass hierarchy. The aligned-LVS source says a light direction need not require hierarchical cosine amplitudes and retains both axions for cosmological predictions. An illustrative reduced potential does not establish a universally valid single-field calculation.

Gauge-sourced extremization, oscillation averaging and infrared convexification answer different questions. The first drops ψ̇ relative to Hψ; the second requires rapid oscillations compared with expansion. Spinodal flattening concerns k→0 and is qualitative here, without a supplied flow scheme or proof of an exactly constant interval for unequal minima.

samples.question: The mixed axion kinetic matrix is diagonalized and canonically normalized numerically at selected t_1,t_2. The resulting mass hierarchy is used to eliminate the heavy axion combination and extract an effective light-field decay constant.

cases.prompt: Which distinct mechanisms generate neutrino masses, and how can extra dimensions or quantum-gravity arguments constrain them?
cases.reviewedTitle: Neutrino mass origins and tests: symmetries, extra dimensions and quantum gravity

sourceBackedScope.text: The sources support a neutrino-mass core with overlapping branches for symmetry-based mechanisms, bulk neutrinos, conjectural scale relations and observable tests. Quark kinetic-term emergence and finite family symmetries instead address charged-fermion hierarchies. The effective-PQ outside candidate merits overlapping membership through its explicit neutrino-mass/dark-matter connection; the heterotic PQ/flavor candidate lacks an explicit neutrino question here. These are organizational connections between questions, not identifications of mechanisms.

scopeLimits.text: Enhanced B−L assumes three Dirac neutrinos and relaxed right-handed charge quantization. Neutrinos remain massless while this enhanced gauge symmetry is unbroken; masses require sub-eV breaking, associated here with a gravitational condensate. Stronger decay constraints than baryonic fifth-force tests require large enhancement and a gauge boson lighter than the heaviest neutrino.

TeV-scale TSSM lacks the large mass scale needed for its conventional high-scale seesaw. The Dark Dimension source distinguishes bulk anomaly inflow from extra brane states, and Green–Schwarz from Higgs gauge-boson mass generation. Its favored Higgs option obtains the stated active-neutrino mass result only after including the full bulk tower.

The emergence source relates neutrino and electroweak scales to the cosmological constant using additional AdS non-SUSY and/or AdS Distance conjectures. Supersymmetry is optional; the quoted gravitino bound also assumes a bound on the superpotential. These conditional scale arguments do not independently verify the detailed mass mechanism.

sampledDistinctions.text: Dirac versus Majorana is separate from seesaw or loop generation: the thesis explicitly discusses Dirac seesaws and radiative masses. The effective-PQ example links a symmetry remnant to a scotogenic sector, but its supplied excerpts do not establish neutrino mass type. A global PQ symmetry also differs from the enhanced gauged B−L construction.

Shared loops, symmetry constraints or emergent kinetic terms do not establish a common physical question. The quark-emergence and finite-family-group facets concern charged-fermion hierarchy. The tower/emergence member explicitly includes neutrino scales and supplies a useful bridge to that neighboring subject.

Bulk mass generation and experimental discrimination deserve separate, linked branches. KATRIN's proposed spectrum can contain several kinks for small bulk mass relative to the compactification scale, or effectively one for large bulk mass. Shared Dark Dimension geometry does not establish that this probe and the bulk B−L construction use identical models or allowed parameters.

sourceBackedScope.text: The supported core combines fixed-t positivity, elastic helicity preparation, massive-state factorization and explicit Regge pole sums. These are complementary methods with different assumptions. The supplied crossing-odd residue construction fits an adjacent spectral branch, where its auxiliary sum must remain distinguished from a Wilson coefficient. Membership follows from the demonstrated operations; several broader description clauses still lack decisive source context.

scopeLimits.text: The QED relation uses massless kinematics s+u+t=0 and positive forward discontinuities for elastic scattering in both crossed channels. Indefinite photon/graviton states must be normalized, with the final bra conjugate to the initial ket. Their elastic matrix element combines definite-helicity components before all-channel pole subtraction.

The displayed undeformed Virasoro–Shapiro example assumes Λ²<1/α′ and gives graviton-pole cancellation without an O(t⁰) term. The factorization construction initially neglects massless exchange and assumes gravity-completing Regge states contribute subdominantly to four-photon scattering. These are distinct treatments of gravitational effects.

The crossing-odd contour subtracts the linear term to regularize the integrand at the origin, also removing a possible gauge z/t pole. Its forward limit is t→0⁻. Convergence and vanishing boundary terms invoke Eq. (8), whose precise growth assumption is absent from the packet.

sampledDistinctions.text: Forward coefficient positivity and spectral residue constraints share contour operations but have different outputs. The crossing-odd auxiliary sum is explicitly not a Wilson coefficient extracted from the amplitude. It warrants a spectral-sum-rule branch alongside coefficient bounds.

Fakeon average continuation removes absorptive contributions from fakeon-containing loops; compatibility with the core dispersion premises is unestablished here. Lee–Wick's n=2 pole diagnoses quadratic ultraviolet divergence in an on-shell mass shift, distinct from a four-dimensional logarithmic pole. Shared loop techniques do not establish common analyticity assumptions.

Density-fluctuation amplitudes describe cosmological evolution; ghost-condensate dispersion describes frequency–momentum propagation; the Newton beta function evolves a coupling. Their amplitude, dispersion and ultraviolet vocabulary does not establish membership in scattering contour or factorization methods.

cases.prompt: How does a boundary description account for bulk gravity and black-hole information, and where do AdS and de Sitter constructions differ?
requiredDistinctions: boundary unitarity versus an imported conjecture
cases.reviewedTitle: Holographic quantum gravity: boundary descriptions, information bounds and consistency

sourceBackedScope.text: Five sampled members directly support distinct branches for proposed dS/CFT, conditional AdS dual admissibility, regulated information bounds, matter interactions and black-hole unitarity. They form a useful umbrella without sharing one derivation or regime. The outside de Sitter lectures fit as scoped foundational material. The dark-bubble review merits provisional adjacent membership because its overview explicitly connects holography to its gravity-localization question; the relevant section remains unsupplied.

scopeLimits.text: dS/CFT is a proposal that permits non-unitarity and complex conformal weights. Its two asymptotic boundaries map antipodally to a single sphere. The observer-past region instead has a planar dual, with bulk time evolution related to boundary scale transformations; the central-charge analysis concerns dS3.

The scale-separation obstruction assumes a CFT obtained by decoupling brane degrees of freedom from ambient gravity. Its precise target is violation of an asymptotic condition along a scalar-potential gradient trajectory involving the quantum-gravity cutoff. Preserve that assumption and the authors' conditional claim.

The matter example uses ℓ_AdS^(d−1)/G_N ∼ N ≫ 1, sparse low-dimension operators and a higher-spin gap. Stress-tensor correlators retain large-N factorization while selected matter correlators need not; an order-one matter three-point function is the stated target.

sampledDistinctions.text: Scale separation and strong matter interactions are different questions. A brane-decoupling constraint on candidate AdS duals does not establish a constraint on matter factorization. Likewise, the higher-spin gap invoked for a semiclassical matter dual is not identified here with the scale-separation condition.

The BTZ discussion distinguishes finite-k quasi-periodicity from exponential decay as L_eff ∼ kL becomes infinite in the semiclassical limit. Classical AdS3 quotient classification instead concerns topology, horizons and causal restrictions. Shared black-hole or wormhole terminology establishes no derivation between these questions.

An induced 4D Einstein metric on a dark bubble does not by itself specify a boundary CFT. The review announces a holographic explanation for why localization is unnecessary; the outside candidate develops force modification and cosmology through 5D backreaction. These support adjacent, separately scoped questions.
